Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class CertificateController

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.CertificateController
All Implemented Interfaces:
CertificatesApi
@RestController public class CertificateController extends Object implements CertificatesApi
Manages the client certificates bound to the authenticated account (the operations of the contract). Binding and unbinding change how the account signs in, so both call StepUpGuard first, as unlinking an identity does. The controller exists whether or not the sign-in with a certificate is enabled, so certificates can be bound before it is turned on.

    • bindCertificate

      public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Certificate> bindCertificate(BindCertificateRequest request)
      Binds a certificate to the authenticated account.
      Specified by:
      bindCertificate in interface CertificatesApi
      Parameters:
      request - the PEM certificate.
      Returns:
      201 Created with the binding.
      Throws:
      InvalidCertificateException - if the value is not a usable certificate.
      CertificateAlreadyBoundException - if the certificate is bound to another account.
      InsufficientUserAuthenticationException - if the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a recent multi-factor sign-in.

    • unbindCertificate

      public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> unbindCertificate(UUID id)
      Unbinds a certificate of the authenticated account.
      Specified by:
      unbindCertificate in interface CertificatesApi
      Parameters:
      id - identifier of the binding.
      Returns:
      204 No Content.
      Throws:
      CertificateNotFoundException - if the account has no such certificate.
      LastSignInMethodException - if the certificate is the last way the account can sign in.
      InsufficientUserAuthenticationException - if the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a recent multi-factor sign-in.
